searchText: has anyone thought about unbundling attacks in ePBS yet? I think it is potentially relevant to the design of the postSignedEnvelope API: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/580#discussion_r2887819954 Regarding the scenario which you have described in the comment, I think the builder would publish the block after the attestation deadline. So the builder could have a view on which block has gained enough weight and release the payload if the block that has commited to their bid has gained the most weight or is the most likely the become canonical? so I would release the payload only if Block A has gained enough attestations otherwise I can honestly withold my payload if block B becomes canonical I think the fact that the builder can now wait and see if the beacon block which includes their bids gains enough attestations before releasing their payload makes unbundling attacks difficult in ePBS? yeah that's a good point do you think it's OK to externalise that check onto the builder, or should it be built-in to the BN's endpoint? All the builders as far as i know rely on the beacon apis to broadcast their beacon block today, they don't directly gossip on the p2p network. A serious builder would also be super well connected in the p2p n/w and can detect equivocating blocks pretty fast. I think it makes sense to have a `broadcast_validation=equivocation` while broadcasting so that builders can be 100% safe from unbundling? A builder could also submit a slashing proof in this case I guess? but I don't think the builder would get the reward yeah nah whistleblower rewards do not exist (it always goes to the proposer that includes the slashing) We've been thinking quite a bit and the worst complications on forkchoice are due to it I believe. What would be your concern? Ah need to read your comment Yes the equivocation you describe in that comment <@602753420033785856> is specifically what led to `should_apply_proposer_boost` and similar changes where we now need to track equivocations live

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: has anyone thought about unbundling attacks in ePBS yet? I think it is potentially relevant to the design of the postSignedEnvelope API: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/580#discussion_r2887819954

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content: Regarding the scenario which you have described in the comment, I think the builder would publish the block after the attestation deadline. So the builder could have a view on which block has gained enough weight and release the payload if the block that has commited to their bid has gained the most weight or is the most likely the become canonical?

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content: so I would release the payload only if Block A has gained enough attestations otherwise I can honestly withold my payload if block B becomes canonical

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content: I think the fact that the builder can now wait and see if the beacon block which includes their bids gains enough attestations before releasing their payload makes unbundling attacks difficult in ePBS?

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content:
yeah that's a good point

do you think it's OK to externalise that check onto the builder, or should it be built-in to the BN's endpoint?

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content:
All the builders as far as i know rely on the beacon apis to broadcast their beacon block today, they don't directly gossip on the p2p network. 
A serious builder would also be super well connected in the p2p n/w and can detect equivocating blocks pretty fast. 
I think it makes sense to have a `broadcast_validation=equivocation` while broadcasting so that builders can be 100% safe from unbundling?

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content: A builder could also submit a slashing proof in this case I guess? but I don't think the builder would get the reward

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: yeah nah whistleblower rewards do not exist (it always goes to the proposer that includes the slashing)

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: We've been thinking quite a bit and the worst complications on forkchoice are due to it I believe. What would be your concern?
